name: Content-Digest carries SHA-256 and sha-256 (uppercase dictionary key is not a case-insensitive synonym)
spec_reference: #verifier-checklist-requests step 1 (RFC 9530 §2 Content-Digest is an RFC 8941 Dictionary; RFC 8941 §3.1.2 keys are lowercase only)
$comment: RFC 9530 §2 Content-Digest is an RFC 8941 Dictionary, and the RFC 8941 §3.1.2 key production admits lowercase characters only (a-z, 0-9, '_', '-', '.', '*'; first character a-z or '*'). 'SHA-256' is therefore a parse-invalid key (RFC 8941 §4.2.3.3: parsing fails when the first character is not lcalpha or '*'), not a case-insensitive synonym of 'sha-256' and not a second spelling of the same algorithm. Verifiers MUST NOT fold case to reconcile the two members. Grading is on the error code, so a folding verifier that reports a duplicate algorithm still returns the expected code; this vector catches verifiers that ignore the unknown key or compare keys as written and accept the header, after which a signer and verifier may disagree on which value entered the signature base. Verifier MUST reject at step 1. Both members carry the correct sha-256 of the body so the digest value itself is not the fault; sibling of 023-multi-valued-content-digest (same algorithm twice, same spelling).
